rounds.proof_sketch: For input shape [128, 4000], whether dim=0 (inner_size=4000) or dim=1 (inner_size=1): kernel launches with block=dim3(inner_size), so threadIdx.x ∈ [0, inner_size-1]. Thus inner_idx = threadIdx.x is always < inner_size. Original condition 'inner_idx >= inner_size' evaluates to false (since inner_size-1 < inner_size). Mutated condition 'inner_idx >= inner_size + 1' also evaluates to false (since inner_size-1 < inner_size+1). Both guards are always false, so mutation has no effect.
rounds.survival_reason: The kernel launch configuration explicitly sets blockDim.x = inner_size, which means threadIdx.x is constrained by CUDA to the range [0, inner_size-1]. The original boundary check 'inner_idx >= inner_size' was already unreachable dead code because threadIdx.x can never equal or exceed blockDim.x. Changing the threshold to 'inner_idx >= inner_size + 1' makes the condition even harder to trigger, but since it was already impossible to trigger, both versions behave identically. All valid threads pass both guards and execute the same cumulative product logic. No input values can change this thread-index arithmetic.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable - the mutation affects an unreachable branch. CUDA guarantees threadIdx.x < blockDim.x = inner_size, so the guard 'inner_idx >= inner_size' is always false. Loosening to 'inner_idx >= inner_size + 1' keeps the condition unreachable. No value-level input can trigger this path.
rounds.recommendations: Boundary checks of the form 'threadIdx.x >= blockDim.x' are inherently dead code because CUDA enforces thread indices stay within launch bounds. Mutation testing tools should recognize this CUDA-specific equivalence pattern. Kernel authors should either remove redundant guards or document them as defensive programming that cannot be triggered under normal execution.
